problem_statement: Federated multi-label classification suffers from label co-occurrence heterogeneity: each client observes different local label relationships, so naive global aggregation can amplify local spurious correlations while ignoring reliable semantic or domain knowledge about labels.
existing_weakness: Existing designs often treat label graphs as extra branches, posterior statistics, or fully data-driven correlations. This makes the graph easy to contaminate with client-specific bias and makes personalization rely on either parameter distance or complete graph distance, including high-confidence common-sense edges that should not dominate client differences.
method_summary: FedGraphHarmony constructs a confidence-aware prior label graph from label semantics and external knowledge, converts the global graph into a label-token attention communication mask, preserves reliable relations through confidence-weighted soft constraints, extracts local graphs only from prior-debiased data-only attention evidence, updates the global graph mainly through low-confidence edges, and performs personalized aggregation using low-confidence structural residuals. The main principle is: high-confidence relations are anchored, low-confidence relations are allowed to adapt.
contributions: Confidence-aware prior label graph from semantic similarity and external knowledge.
Graph mask injected directly into label-token attention scores, rather than an extra GCN branch.
Prior-debiased local graph extraction from data-only attention evidence.
Confidence-weighted KL soft constraint to keep reliable edges stable while relaxing uncertain edges.
Personalized federated aggregation based on low-confidence structural residuals.
